ModMetaData.name: Wardrobe Attendant
ModMetaData.author: TerrorVanHoover
ModMetaData.description:
Assign colonists and eligible colony mechanoids to continuously maintain the required apparel of colonists, slaves, prisoners, colony animals and colony mechanoids.
Features: - Create multiple apparel rules per pawn. - Full outfit mode: automatically find and equip the best permitted apparel. - Exact item mode: search only for the selected apparel def; other apparel sharing its layers does not interfere with selection. - Reorder apparel rules directly in the Wardrobe window. Slot order determines the order in which rules are evaluated: rules higher in the list are serviced first. Exact item rules take priority over Full outfit rules when both can apply to the same apparel. - Active wardrobe jobs respect slot reordering. If a higher-priority rule becomes applicable after a slot is moved, an active ForceTargetWear or self-wear job is revalidated and cancelled when its selected apparel is no longer the highest-priority candidate. Compatible higher-priority rules do not interrupt an active job, and jobs are reissued according to the new slot order. Pending lock-job references are updated so saves made during an active job restore the correct rule after loading. - Filter apparel by quality range and durability threshold. - Per-slot option to allow or forbid a pawn from servicing their own wardrobe. - Per-slot early replacement: a substantially better available item can replace current apparel before it reaches the durability threshold. - Per-slot option to allow or forbid Wardrobe Attendant workers from removing locked apparel. - Apparel is scored using quality, condition and actual armor ratings. Market value is not used. - Protection scoring always includes condition and uses normalized cold and heat insulation, toxicity resistance and vacuum resistance. Vacuum protection receives the strongest weight, followed by toxicity protection. - Configure protection priorities for Full outfit and Exact item rules: cold protection, heat protection, armor, toxicity protection and vacuum protection. When protection priorities are enabled, only the selected protection weights are used. - Vanilla self-equipping is prevented from re-equipping apparel that Wardrobe Attendant recently displaced through early replacement. - Vanilla self-equipping is prevented from selecting below-threshold apparel when a suitable replacement is available. - Self-service uses a dedicated self-wear path and respects the same outfit policy, protection, durability, corpse and locked-apparel rules. - Optionally mark suitable apparel as forced after it is equipped by a Wardrobe Attendant job. The player can still remove or replace it manually; workers respect the slot's locked-apparel removal setting. The lock decision is bound to the apparel rule that issued the job: its current "lock after equipping" setting at the moment of equipping decides both the vanilla padlock and the forced-apparel entry. Other rules do not affect it. Toggling the setting while a job is in progress correctly changes the outcome at the moment of equipping. Self-service always drops conflicting apparel to the ground instead of removing it silently. - Optionally replace apparel after it falls below its durability threshold and a better permitted replacement is available. - Optionally remove apparel after it falls below its durability threshold when no compatible replacement is available. A worker removes all eligible worn-out items in one visit, only after completing the removal work. Interrupting the work does not remove apparel. - Exact apparel rules can replace their required apparel with a better item of the same apparel def after it falls below the durability threshold. The currently worn same-def item is treated as the replacement target, not as a conflicting item. - Exact apparel rules can remove their required apparel after it falls below the durability threshold when no permitted replacement is available. - Exact apparel rules protect their required apparel from being removed or replaced by full outfit rules. - When multiple Exact item rules apply, a higher-priority Exact item rule can displace conflicting apparel assigned to a lower-priority Exact item rule; lower-priority rules cannot displace apparel required by higher-priority rules. - Full outfit rules do not remove or replace apparel required by exact item rules. - If the only apparent replacement for worn apparel is protected by an exact item rule, the worn apparel can still be removed according to its own removal settings. - Workers respect outfit policies, reservations, reachability, burning items, body compatibility and apparel restrictions. - Full outfit jobs evaluate candidates against the currently worn outfit before issuing one dressing job at a time. - Replacement checks and full outfit job selection share the same conflict checks; unrelated clothing does not count as a replacement for a worn-out item. - Exact apparel availability checks use the selected rule's quality and condition filters, the pawn's apparel policy, wearability, reservations and reachability. - Full outfit rules leave apparel defs assigned to enabled exact item rules to those exact item rules. - Wardrobe configuration is available for colony prisoners even when they belong to another faction. - Empty or invalid exact item rules are disabled on load and remain exact item rules; they never become full outfit rules automatically. - Exact item rules whose selected apparel cannot currently be worn by the assigned pawn are marked as unfulfillable. They retain their configuration, display a warning icon, and are excluded from wardrobe servicing and apparel protection until the item becomes wearable again. For humanlike pawns, an exact item remains selectable when its required body part groups exist in the race body definition and can potentially be restored; selecting it shows an explanation. - Exact item selectors display apparel that a humanlike pawn cannot currently wear when its required body part groups exist in the pawn's race body definition and can potentially be restored. Such entries display a warning icon and show an explanation when selected. Colony animals use vanilla body-part wearability checks for their exact apparel lists. - Optionally allow corpse-worn apparel, optionally restrict a rule to corpse-worn apparel only, while always respecting the pawn's vanilla apparel policy. Corpse-worn apparel settings apply independently to each apparel rule. - A slot restricted to corpse-worn apparel replaces or removes currently worn non-corpse apparel when a suitable corpse-worn replacement is or is not available. - Duplicate dressing and removal jobs are avoided through job, reservation and cached active-job checks. - Compatible with animal apparel and modded races through RimWorld's apparel wearability checks. - The Wardrobe button highlights green when a pawn has at least one enabled apparel slot. - Works with existing saves: safely enables, disables and normalizes saved wardrobe assignments. - Optimized job scanning with cached wardrobe assignments, cached active-job checks, per-tick map apparel caching, cached exact item candidates, cached apparel scoring, reusable protected and available exact apparel caches, reusable UI listings and reduced temporary allocations. Periodic pending-job cleanup runs independently of job scanning. Apparel removal uses RimWorld's built-in toil duration counter, with saved progress and compatibility with the previous removal progress format. - Optional compatibility setting: prevent vanilla self-equipping from selecting apparel that an enabled Wardrobe Attendant rule is set to remove. - Pending wardrobe jobs are owned by their issuing job and are cleared after successful completion; cancellation and failure retain their short cooldown. - Apparel removal is revalidated immediately before the worker changes the target's equipment. In batch removal jobs, every eligible apparel item is validated separately, so items with an available replacement remain equipped. - Apparel equipping is revalidated immediately before the target actually wears the selected item. The selected item is validated directly, including apparel already carried by the worker, so an item that no longer matches its rule, policy or protected apparel restrictions is not equipped. - Wardrobe jobs are revalidated when the worker reaches the target and periodically during work, preventing unnecessary waiting or work when apparel or rules have become invalid. - Wear jobs are revalidated immediately before the worker begins unequipping conflicting apparel, then again during final apparel wearing validation. This avoids a global Harmony patch on JobDriver.DriverTick and reduces compatibility risk with other mods. - Apparel that fails an enabled rule's quality or condition filter is treated as a removal candidate even when its durability remains above the configured threshold. - A valid replacement cancels removal of apparel that fails the rule's quality filter, even when its durability remains above the configured threshold. - Optional setting: skip drafted colonists when selecting new Wardrobe Attendant targets. Already active Wardrobe Attendant jobs targeting a drafted colonist are interrupted before equipment is changed. - While removing apparel, the target pawn is held in place for the duration of the removal work, without overriding a player-forced order. - Localized UI through RimWorld translation files. - Optional detailed diagnostics for wardrobe job selection, wear validation, full outfit candidate checks and job completion.
Wardrobe maintenance is performed through a separate Wardrober work type. Hauling must be available to enable Wardrober for a pawn, but can be disabled afterward. - Wardrober can be enabled or disabled separately from Hauling. - The Wardrober checkbox is available only to colony colonists, colony slaves and eligible colony mechanoids whose Hauling work is available. - Colony mechanoids also require Manipulation to perform Wardrober work. - Prisoners and animals cannot perform Wardrober work, but can still be configured as wardrobe targets. - Colony mechanoids can be configured as wardrobe targets when they are wearing apparel. This excludes vanilla transport drones and other mechanoids without worn apparel. - Optional compatibility with Man-at-arms: its humanoid mechanoids remain valid wardrobe targets even when not wearing apparel. The compatibility check uses cached reflection and safely falls back to the standard worn-apparel check if Man-at-arms is absent or changes its API. - Optional compatibility with Mech Work Tab: Wardrober is shown as a work column for colony mechanoids, and its tooltip uses the standard work-type tooltip. The compatibility patch is applied only when Mech Work Tab is loaded. - Wardrobe UI for eligible colony mechanoids uses the vanilla Gear tab, like animals. No fallback gizmo is added. - Lock after equipping works for eligible colony mechanoids when outfit tracking is available and is a safe no-op otherwise. - The mod does not patch MechanitorUtility.AnyPlayerMechCanDoWork; vanilla control groups and work type visibility are unaffected. - A compatibility guard prevents thought queries for mechanoids without mood or thought context. This avoids NullReferenceException errors in UI mods such as NiceInventoryTab when opening the Gear tab on a mechanoid. - Compatible with colony children, enslaved children, imprisoned children and young colony animals as wardrobe targets. - Only one active Full outfit rule is allowed per pawn; enabling another Full outfit rule deactivates the previous one. - Only one active Exact item rule for the same apparel def is allowed per pawn; enabling another identical Exact item rule deactivates the previous one. - The first apparel slot is created as an active Full outfit rule. - Second and subsequent apparel slots are created as active Exact item rules without a selected apparel def. - Attempting to activate a duplicate Full outfit or duplicate identical Exact item rule deactivates the new slot and shows a warning.
